prompt: Complete CsvTableStore so save writes a header row plus data rows as CSV, loadHeader returns the first line's fields and loadRows returns everything after it.
explanation: Files.write(Path, Iterable<CharSequence>, Charset) writes each element as its own line and appends the platform line separator, which pairs naturally with Files.readAllLines on the way back in. String.join(",", fields) builds a line without the trailing-separator bug a manual loop invites. Passing -1 as the limit to split keeps trailing empty fields instead of silently dropping them, so a row ending in an empty column still has the right number of fields.
hints: Collect the header line and the row lines into a List<String>, then hand that whole list to Files.write.
String.join(",", array) turns a String[] into one comma-separated line.
loadRows should start its loop at index 1 so the header line is skipped; a one-line file then yields an empty list.
